==Problem==
An equilateral triangle and a regular hexagon have equal perimeters. If the triangle's area is 4, what is the area of the hexagon?

<math> \textbf{(A)}\hspace{.05in}4\qquad\textbf{(B)}\hspace{.05in}5\qquad\textbf{(C)}\hspace{.05in}6\qquad\textbf{(D)}\hspace{.05in}4\sqrt3\qquad\textbf{(E)}\hspace{.05in}6\sqrt3 </math>

==Solution 1 (recommended)==
Let the perimeter of the equilateral triangle be <imath> 3s </imath>. The side length of the equilateral triangle would then be <imath> s </imath> and the sidelength of the hexagon would be <imath> \frac{s}{2} </imath>.

A hexagon contains six equilateral triangles. One of these triangles would be similar to the large equilateral triangle in the ratio <imath> 1 : 4 </imath>, since the sidelength of the small equilateral triangle is half the side length of the large one. Thus, the area of one of the small equilateral triangles is <imath> 1 </imath>. The area of the hexagon is then <imath> 1 \times 6 = \boxed{\textbf{(C)}\ 6} </imath>.

==Solution 2 (Hard)==
Let the side length of the small triangle be <imath>2x</imath>, so the side length of the hexagon is <imath>x</imath>. By the Pythagorean theorem, the height of the triangle is <imath>x\sqrt{3}</imath>, so the area of the triangle is <imath>\frac{x^2}{\sqrt{3}}</imath> We are given that the area is <imath>4</imath>, so x must be <imath>\frac{2}{\sqrt[4]{3}}</imath>. Therefore, by the Pythagorean theorem, the height of one of the triangles in the hexagon (made by subdividing the hexagon into <imath>6</imath> congruent triangles), is <imath>\frac{\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt[4]{3}}</imath>, so the area is <imath>\frac{\frac{2}{\sqrt[4]{3}}\times\frac{\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt[4]{3}}}{2}</imath>, which equals <imath>1</imath>. Since there are <imath>6</imath> such triangles in the hexagon, the area of the hexagon is <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(C)}\ 6}</imath>.

==Solution 3 (Formula)==
The area of an equilateral triangle is <imath>\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} a^2</imath>, where a is the side. Since a hexagon is six equilateral triangles combined, the area of a hexagon is <imath>\left(\frac{3\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) a^2</imath>. If we assume the side of the hexagon is 1, and the side of the triangle is <imath>2</imath>(perimeter is the same but sides are 6:3), then the area of the triangle will be <imath>4\sqrt{3}</imath>. We killed it is a <imath>\sqrt{3} : 4</imath> ratio of the assumed triangle area to the actual triangle area. This indicates the area of the hexagon will also be a ratio of <imath>\sqrt{3} : 4</imath>, so the area of the assumed hexagon is <imath>\frac{3\sqrt{3}}{2}</imath>. Therefore, the area of the actual hexagon will be <imath>\frac{\frac{3\sqrt{3}}{2} \cdot 4}{\sqrt{3}}</imath>. Simplifying the result will give us <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(C)}\ 6}</imath>.
